correctness.rationale: Exact geometric identity: all eight cube projected vertices have squared norm 3-(v·U)²; ordering the absolute normal coordinates reduces the smallest signed sum to |c-a-b|. Haar sphere splits into 48 sign/order chambers; spherical coordinates with θ≤atan(secφ) have area density (12/π)sinθ. The strictly decreasing cosθ-(sinφ+cosφ)sinθ yields the two exhaustive threshold intervals; their elementary cosine endpoints integrate to B(t)+J(t) without losing mass. At t*=1/√3 the second branch turns on with coefficient 9sqrt3/(4π), yielding the jump 36sqrt3/π in the second derivative in radius; an independent six-axis diamond expansion and four transverse great-circle strips establish both endpoint coefficients. All hypotheses, normalization and endpoints are explicit. The standalone packaged checker passed with independent vertex projection reconstruction, 2D spherical quadrature, endpoint and phase diagnostics; numerical experiments corroborate, not replace, proof.

originality.rationale: Originality comparison is statement-level. Previously published exact diameter law of octahedron sections is polar-dual to cube-shadow **inradius**, not cube-shadow **circumradius**. The exact inradius law for octahedron projections is dual to cube **section** radius, not cube **projection** radius. Known 3-cube width laws, shadow area/perimeter moments, cube-projection face counts, and high-dimensional asymptotics do not imply the exact fixed-three-dimensional shadow circumradius CDF or its second-derivative transition. Relevant full primary mathematical claims inspected; historical priority is best-knowledge rather than exhaustive.
residual_risks: An equivalent law for minimum signed sums of three spherical coordinates, or fixed 3D cube shadow diameters, might be published under a different name or unindexed historical source.
Primary PDF sections were inspected for their relevant theorem claims; lack of a matching keyword alone was not treated as proof of noncoverage.
Published results on correlated widths might conceivably imply a harder formula if their full joint law is known; no such stronger theorem was located.

value.rationale: Circumradius is the natural minimal enclosing-circle metric of an entire Haar-random planar zonogon shadow of the cube, which was not determined by earlier face vectors, scalar 1D widths, or area/perimeter moments. The claim gives its complete probability distribution with sharp support and two distinct endpoint scaling laws and identifies a structural C¹-but-not-C² transition when a second type of farthest-vertex configuration becomes feasible. A full CDF with a nontrivial geometric threshold is a motivated self-contained random convex geometry result, not a routine moment or arbitrary finite slice.
